prov.heading: Provision for Credit Losses
prov.text:
Management actively monitors the Company’s asset quality and provides specific loss provisions when necessary. Provisions for credit losses are charged to income to bring the total allowance for credit losses on loans and off-balance sheet credit exposures to a level deemed appropriate by management of the Company based on such factors as historical lifetime credit loss experience, the amount of nonperforming loans and related collateral, the volume growth and composition of the loan portfolio, current economic conditions and reasonable and supportable forecasted economic conditions that may affect borrower ability to pay and the value of collateral, the evaluation of the loan portfolio through the internal loan review process and other relevant factors.

Loans are charged off against the allowance for credit losses when appropriate. Although management believes it uses the best information available to make determinations with respect to the provision for credit losses, future adjustments may be necessary if economic conditions differ from the assumptions used in making the initial determinations.

There was no provision for credit losses for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025.

Net charge-offs were $4.4 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 compared with net charge-offs of $6.5 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025.

nonint.heading: Noninterest Expense
nonint.text:
Noninterest expense totaled $308.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared with $138.6 million for the same period in 2025, an increase of $170.0 million or 122.6%, primarily due to increases in merger related expenses, salaries and benefits and additional expenses related to the Mergers. Noninterest expense totaled $702.1 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared with $417.5 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of $284.6 million or 68.2%, primarily due to an increase in merger related expenses of $113.0 million, an increase in salaries and benefits and an increase in additional expenses related to nine months of American operations, eight months of Southwest operations and three months of Stellar operations.

pretax.text: Net interest income before the provision for credit losses was $443.0 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 an increase of $169.5 million or 62.0% compared with $273.4 million for the same period in 2025. The net interest margin on a tax-equivalent basis was 3.73% for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 an increase of 49 basis points compared with 3.24% for the same period in 2025. The changes to both measures were primarily due to the impact of the Mergers, the repricing of assets, and a decrease in the average balance and average rate on other borrowings.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
The amount of federal and state income tax expense is influenced by the amount of pre-tax income, the amount of tax-exempt income and the amount of nondeductible expenses. Income tax expense totaled $45.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared with $38.5 million for the same period in 2025, an increase of $7.1 million or 18.6%. Income tax expense totaled $126.2 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared with $111.6 million for the same period in 2025, an increase of $14.6 million or 13.1%. The Company’s effective tax rate for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025 was 24.4% and 21.9%, respectively. The Company’s effective tax rate for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, and 2025 was 22.8% and 21.7%, respectively. The increase in provision for income taxes and effective tax rate was primarily due to an increase in nondeductible merger related expenses for the Mergers and an out of state tax settlement.

Enactment of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act — On July 4, 2025, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (the “OBBB Act”), which included certain modifications to U.S. tax law, was enacted.

net.text: For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, net income available to common shareholders was $141.5 million or $1.18 per diluted common share compared with $137.6 million or $1.45 for the same period in 2025. Net income and net income per diluted common share for the third quarter of 2026 were primarily impacted by an increase in net interest income due to the Mergers, partially offset by an increase in merger related expenses, an increase in noninterest expenses related to the Mergers and an increase in provision for income taxes due to an increase in nondeductible merger related expenses and an out of state tax settlement. The $5.0 million tax settlement resulted in a higher than normal effective tax rate of 24.4%. The Company posted annualized returns on average common equity of 5.77% and 7.18%, annualized returns on average assets of 1.06% and 1.44% and efficiency ratios of 62.05% and 44.06% for the quarters ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. The efficiency ratio is calculated by dividing total noninterest expense (excluding net gains and losses on the sale, write-down or write-up of assets and securities) by the sum of net interest income and noninterest income.

wc.text: Included in commercial and industrial loans are (1) commitments to oil and gas producers largely secured by proven, developed and producing reserves and (2) commitments to service, equipment and midstream companies secured mainly by accounts receivable, inventory and equipment. Mineral reserve values supporting commitments to producers are normally re-determined semi-annually using reserve studies prepared by a third-party and verified by the Company’s oil and gas engineer. Accounts receivable and inventory borrowing bases for service companies are typically re-determined monthly. Funding requests by both producers and service companies are monitored relative to the most recently determined borrowing base.

capex.text: The Company has no exposure to future cash requirements associated with known uncertainties or capital expenditures of a material nature.

Net interest income.heading: Net Interest Income
Net interest income.text: The Company’s net interest income is affected by changes in the amount and mix of interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities, referred to as a “volume change.” It is also affected by changes in yields earned on interest-earning assets and rates paid on interest-bearing deposits and other borrowed funds, referred to as a “rate change.”

Noninterest income.heading: Noninterest Income
Noninterest income.text:
The Company’s primary sources of recurring noninterest income are credit, debit and ATM card income, nonsufficient funds fees and service charges on deposit accounts. Additionally, the Company generates recurring noninterest income from its various additional products and services, including trust services, mortgage lending, brokerage and independent sales organization sponsorship operations. Noninterest income does not include loan origination fees, which are recognized over the life of the related loan as an adjustment to yield using the interest method.

Noninterest income totaled $52.7 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared with $41.2 million for the same period in 2025, an increase of $11.5 million or 27.8%, primarily due to the Mergers, partially offset by a net loss on the sale and write-down of assets. Noninterest income totaled $159.9 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared with $125.5 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of $34.4 million or 27.4%, primarily due to the Mergers and a gain on the Visa Class B-2 stock exchange net of investment securities sales of $9.2 million.

intro.text: Prosperity Bancshares, Inc. ® , a Texas corporation (the “Company”), was formed in 1983 as a vehicle to acquire the former Allied Bank in Edna, Texas, which was chartered in 1949 as The First National Bank of Edna and is now known as Prosperity Bank. The Company is a registered financial holding company that derives substantially all of its revenues and income from the operation of its bank subsidiary, Prosperity Bank ® (“Prosperity Bank ® ” or the “Bank”). The Bank provides a wide array of financial products and services to businesses and consumers throughout Texas and Oklahoma.

accounts.note: Depreciation and amortisation includes the amortisation of intangibles where the filing reports one line: the PP&E residual then carries the intangibles' share.

accounts.name: Goodwill and intangibles
accounts.note: Acquisitions add goodwill and intangibles at their allocated values, not at the cash paid; the residual is the difference and the amortisation.

accounts.name: Equity
accounts.note: Other comprehensive income (currency translation, unrealised gains) moves equity without passing through net income: it is in the residual.
